source.title: Positivity Problems and Conjectures in Algebraic Combinatorics

accepted.question_text: Let Δ be a Gorenstein* simplicial complex, meaning that for every face σ of Δ, including the empty face, the reduced simplicial homology of the link of σ is that of a sphere of the appropriate dimension. Does the Generalized Lower Bound Theorem, or more generally the g-theorem, hold for Gorenstein* complexes?

evidence.quote: Does the GLBT (or more generally the g-theorem) hold for Gorenstein* complexes?

accepted.question_text: Let P be either an arbitrary convex polytope or, more generally, a Gorenstein poset that is a lattice after removing \hat{0} and \hat{1}. If (h_0, h_1, ..., h_r) is the toric h-vector of P, is the Generalized Lower Bound Theorem inequality h_0 ≤ h_1 ≤ ··· ≤ h_floor(r/2) always true?

evidence.quote: Let P be an arbitrary convex polytope, or even a Gorenstein poset that is a lattice with \hat{0} and \hat{1} removed. For the toric h-vector (h0, h1, …, hr) of P, is the GLBT h0 ≤ h1 ≤ ··· ≤ h⌊r/2⌋ true?

accepted.question_text: Let (h_0, h_1, ..., h_d) be the h-vector of a centrally symmetric polytope of dimension d. Must each entry satisfy h_i ≥ binom(d, i)?
accepted.context_brief: Lower bounds for centrally symmetric h-vectors

evidence.quote: Let (h0, h1, …, hd) be the h-vector of a centrally symmetric polytope. Is it true that hi ≥ \binom{d}{i}?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a finite ranked poset of rank r + 1 such that P minus its minimum and maximum elements is Gorenstein*. Suppose P has a lattice automorphism ν that is an involution and fixes only \hat{0} and \hat{1}. Is the cardinality of P always at least 2r + 1?

evidence.quote: Let P be a finite ranked poset of rank r + 1 such that P − {\hat{0}, \hat{1}} is Gorenstein*. Suppose that P has a lattice automorphism ν that is an involution and that fixes only \hat{0} and \hat{1}. Is it true that |P| ≥ 2r+1?

accepted.question_text: Let Δ be a (2d − 1)-dimensional Gorenstein* flag complex with h-vector (h_0, h_1, ..., h_{2d}). Is the alternating sum constrained by the Charney-Davis inequality (-1)^d(h_0 - h_1 + ··· + h_{2d}) ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Let Δ be a 2d − 1 dimensional Gorenstein* flag complex with h-vector (h0, h1, …, h2d). Is it true that (−1)d(h0 − h1 + ··· + h2d) ≥ 0?

accepted.question_text: Suppose Δ is a finite abstract simplicial complex such that for every face σ of dimension at most k, including the empty face, the link of σ is acyclic. Can Δ, regarded as a poset under inclusion, be partitioned into intervals [F, G] such that every interval satisfies dim G − dim F ≤ k + 1 and the collection of all bottom elements F forms a subcomplex of Δ?

evidence.quote: Suppose that Δ is a (finite) abstract simplicial complex such that the link of every σ ∈ Δ of dimension at most k (including link(∅) = Δ) is acyclic. Can Δ (regarded as a partially ordered set under set inclusion) be partitioned into intervals [F, G] such that (a) dim G − dim F ≤ k + 1, and (b) the bottom elements F of these intervals form a subcomplex of Δ?

accepted.question_text: Is every Cohen-Macaulay simplicial complex partitionable, meaning that a pure simplicial complex can always be partitioned into intervals [F, G] whose top elements G are maximal faces?

evidence.quote: Is every Cohen-Macaulay complex partitionable?

accepted.question_text: If P is a Gorenstein poset, are all coefficients of its cd-index Ψ_P(c, d) nonnegative?

evidence.quote: If P is a Gorenstein poset, then are all coefficients of the cd-index ΨP(c, d) nonnegative?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a pure cubical complex of rank r. (a) If P is a Cohen-Macaulay poset, must every entry of its cubical h-vector be nonnegative? (b) If P is also a Gorenstein poset, must its cubical h-vector satisfy h_0(P) ≤ h_1(P) ≤ ··· ≤ h_{r−1}(P)?

evidence.quote: (a) Let P be a pure cubical complex of rank r. If P is a Cohen-Macaulay poset, then is h(P) ≥ 0 for all i? (b) If P is in addition a Gorenstein poset, then is it true that h0(P) ≤ h1(P) ≤ ··· ≤ hr−1(P)? (Adin [1, p. 7] shows that h = h.)

accepted.question_text: Let the Kronecker product coefficients g_{μνλ} be defined by s_μ * s_ν = Σ_λ g_{μνλ} s_λ, where * is the internal product of symmetric functions. Find a combinatorial interpretation of these coefficients that also yields a combinatorial proof that they are nonnegative.

evidence.quote: Find a combinatorial interpretation of the ‘Kronecker product coefficients’ g_{μνλ}, thereby combinatorially proving that they are nonnegative.

accepted.question_text: Let the Schubert intersection coefficients c_{uv}^w be defined by the product of Schubert polynomials \mathfrak S_u \mathfrak S_v = Σ_w c_{uv}^w \mathfrak S_w. Find a combinatorial interpretation of c_{uv}^w that also gives a combinatorial proof that these coefficients are nonnegative.

evidence.quote: Find a combinatorial interpretation of the ‘Schubert intersection coefficients’ c_{uv}^w, thereby combinatorially proving that they are nonnegative.

accepted.question_text: For the symmetric group S_n, give a combinatorial interpretation of the row sums of its character table, and thereby give a combinatorial proof that these row sums are nonnegative.
accepted.context_brief: Row sums of the S_n character table

evidence.quote: Give a combinatorial interpretation of the row sums of the character table of S_n, thereby combinatorially proving that they are nonnegative.

accepted.question_text: Show that for every pair of partitions λ and μ, the (q,t)-Kostka polynomial K_{λμ}(q,t), defined from the Schur expansion of transformed Macdonald symmetric functions, has only nonnegative coefficients.

evidence.quote: Show that the (q,t)-Kostka polynomial K_{\lambda\mu}(q,t) has nonnegative coefficients.

accepted.question_text: For the ribbon polynomials G_{λ/μ}^{(k)}(x;q) defined by summing over ribbon tableaux with q-weight, (a) give a combinatorial proof that these polynomials are symmetric functions, and (b) when they are expanded in the Schur basis, determine whether all coefficients are polynomials in q with nonnegative integer coefficients.
accepted.context_brief: Ribbon polynomial symmetry and Schur positivity

evidence.quote:
(a) Give a combinatorial proof that the polynomials G_{\lambda/\mu}^{(k)}(x;q) are symmetric functions.
   (b) When G_{\lambda/\mu}^{(k)}(x;q) is expanded in terms of Schur functions, are the coefficients polynomials in q with nonnegative integer coefficients?

accepted.question_text: For any Coxeter group W and any interval u ≤ v in the Bruhat order, are all coefficients of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) nonnegative?

evidence.quote: Are the coefficients of P_{u,v}(q) nonnegative for any Coxeter group W and any u≤v in the Bruhat order of W?

accepted.question_text: When W is a finite or affine Weyl group, especially W = S_n, give a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) that yields a combinatorial proof of their nonnegativity.

evidence.quote: Give a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of P_{u,v}(q) when W is a finite or affine Weyl group, especially W=S_n, thereby combinatorially proving that they are nonnegative.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a totally nonnegative n × n matrix, and let λ be a partition of n. Is the irreducible-character immanant Imm_λ(X) always nonnegative?

evidence.quote: If X is a totally nonnegative n×n matrix and λ⊢n, then is Imm_λ(X)≥ 0?

accepted.question_text: Let μ be a partition of n with length at most m, let λ be a partition of n, and let JT_μ be the Jacobi-Trudi matrix (h_{μ_i-i+j})_{i,j=1}^m. Is the immanant Imm_λ(JT_μ) always Schur-positive?

evidence.quote: If l(μ)≤ m, μ⊢n, and λ⊢n, then is Imm_λ(JT_μ) s-positive?

accepted.question_text: For every monomial character φ of the Hecke algebra H_n(q) and every Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element C'_w, is φ(q^{-ℓ(w)/2} C'_w) a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients, and are those coefficients unimodal and symmetric about q^{-ℓ(w)/2}?

evidence.quote: For every monomial character φ of H_n(q) and every Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element C'_w, is it true that φ(q^{-\ell(w)/2}C'_w) is a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients, and moreover that these coefficients are unimodal and symmetric about q^{-\ell(w)/2}?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a naturally labeled poset, and let W(P,t) = Σ_{π in L(P)} t^{des(π)+1}, where L(P) is the set of linear extensions of P and des(π) counts descents. Are all zeros of W(P,t) real?

evidence.quote: Is W(P,t) real?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a distributive lattice, let c_i be the number of i-element chains in P, and let C(P,t) = Σ c_i t^i be the chain polynomial. Are all zeros of C(P,t) real?

evidence.quote: When P is a distributive lattice, is every zero of C(P,t) real?

accepted.question_text: If P is a (3+1)-free poset and G = inc(P) is its incomparability graph, is the chromatic symmetric function X_G e-positive?

evidence.quote: If P is a (3+1)-free poset and G=operatorname{inc}(P), then is X_G e-positive?

accepted.question_text: If G is a finite claw-free graph, meaning that G has no induced subgraph consisting of one vertex joined to three other vertices and no further edges, is the chromatic symmetric function X_G e-positive?

evidence.quote: If G is a finite claw-free graph, i.e., G has no induced subgraph consisting of one vertex connected to three other vertices (and no further edges), is X_G e-positive?

accepted.question_text: If G is a claw-free graph and I(G,t) = Σ s_i t^i is its stable set polynomial, where s_i counts independent i-element vertex sets, does I(G,t) have only real zeros?

evidence.quote: Does the stable set polynomial I(G,t) of a claw-free graph G have only real zeros?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an n × n real matrix whose columns are all weakly increasing, let J denote the n × n all-ones matrix, and let per denote the permanent. Does the polynomial per(A + tJ) always have only real zeros?

evidence.quote: Let A be an n×n real matrix for which every column is weakly increasing. Does the polynomial per(A+tJ) have only real zeros?

accepted.question_text: Are the following sequences always unimodal or log-concave: (a) the absolute values of the coefficients of the chromatic polynomial of a graph, or more generally the characteristic polynomial of a matroid; (b) the numbers of edge-spanning forests of a graph, or more generally the numbers of independent sets of a matroid; and (c) the numbers of elements of rank i in a geometric lattice?

evidence.quote:
Are the sequences below unimodal or log-concave?
(a) The absolute values of the coefficients of the chromatic polynomial of a graph, or more generally, the characteristic polynomial of a matroid.
(b) The number of edge-spanning forests of a graph, or more generally, the number of independent sets of a matroid.
(c) The number of elements of rank i of a geometric lattice.
